title: The specified completed Hom coefficient comparison is the evaluation transpose
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$. Fix finite coefficient fields $E\subset L$ inside an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, their valuation rings and uniformizers $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,X}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $H_R,H_S$ for the ambient derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $T=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ for ordinary derived extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $C=C_{L/E}$ for the strict-tower integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Let $M,N\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Then $H_R(M,N)$ is derived $t$-complete, so the canonical completion maps $\chi_Z:TZ\xrightarrow{\sim}CZ$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] apply to $Z=M,N,H_R(M,N)$.

Let $\theta^{\mathcal Hom}_{L/E;M,N}:C H_R(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_S(CM,CN)$ denote the specified internal-Hom coefficient-operation comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], the comparison whose rationalization is used to conjugate common-stage morphisms in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. To fix the word "specified", use the chain-Hom normalization in the construction of that comparison, rather than an arbitrary family of the displayed isomorphisms. Explicitly, choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $M$, a K-injective representative $I$ of $N$, and a flat-term K-flat resolution $q:Q\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,I)$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Put $J=I_S(I\otimes_RS)$ with its fixed augmentation $j:I\otimes_RS\to J$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The ordinary chain-Hom map used in the coefficient construction is
$$Q\otimes_RS\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_S^\bullet(P\otimes_RS,J),\qquad x\otimes s\longmapsto\bigl(m\otimes b\longmapsto j(q(x)(m)\otimes sb)\bigr).$$
The completed comparison uses this map, the fixed localized resolution augmentations, and the quotient-map completion units on its Hom output and on its two inputs. These are the units $\chi$ above, with their zero shifted-product components; completion here is the specified strict-tower realization, not an arbitrary isomorphism of derived-limit objects. This fixes the construction before asserting that its transpose is the displayed evaluation composite. The Hom differential and the signed tensor convention are those of [def-pur-hom-complex, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation].

Let $c_{M,N}:T H_R(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_S(TM,TN)$ be the evaluation-transpose comparison of [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change]. These actual maps satisfy
$$
 \theta^{\mathcal Hom}_{L/E;M,N}\circ\chi_{H_R(M,N)}
 =H_S(\chi_M^{-1},\chi_N)\circ c_{M,N}.
$$
Equivalently, after the canonical $\chi$ identifications, the specified Hom coefficient-operation comparison has tensor-Hom transpose
$$
 TM\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}T H_R(M,N)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}T(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(M,N))
 \xrightarrow{T(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N})}TN,
$$
where the first arrow is the ordinary tensor scalar-association map. This is an identification with the specified comparison, not just existence of an evaluation-preserving comparison. For $L=E$ the equality uses the canonical completeness-unit identification $C_{E/E}\cong\operatorname{id}$. For $E\subset L\subset F$, with the specified scalar-extension associators, the direct and successive identified Hom comparisons are equal; their uncurried formulas on homogeneous representatives are both $(m\otimes b,h\otimes s\otimes s')\mapsto h(m)\otimes bss'$, with the same signed Hom-complex evaluation convention. When $H_R(M,N)$ is bounded constructible, the displayed identity and the identity/tower equalities remain true in the raw rationalized categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], including for arbitrary localized morphisms.

proof.text: Work on the fixed small skeleton of the pro-etale site. By the integral constructible definition, $M$ and $N$ are derived complete. Apply the internal-Hom completeness clause of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] with $f=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $W=X$: its only completeness requirement for this clause is completeness of $N$, and its constructible hypotheses hold for $M,N$. Thus $H=H_R(M,N)$ is derived $t$-complete; bounded constructibility of $H$ is not needed. By [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], $S$ is a finite free $R$-module and the specified $\chi_Z:TZ\to CZ$ is invertible and natural for $Z=M,N,H$. Its explicit cone-unit description also identifies the units used in the specified comparison.

proof.text: Use the representatives $P,I,q:Q\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,I)$ and $j:I\otimes_RS\to J$ fixed in the statement. K-flat and K-injective existence are [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Write $d$ for the ordinary coefficient map represented by the chain-Hom formula in the statement. Its $S$-linearity is the balancing identity $q(x)(rm)\otimes sb=q(x)(m)\otimes r sb$, together with linearity in $s,b$. Its compatibility with the Hom differential is immediate by substituting $d(h)=d_Ih-(-1)^{|h|}h d_P$: the two terms become $j(d_Ih(m)\otimes sb)$ and $-(-1)^{|h|}j(h(d_Pm)\otimes sb)$ on both sides. Scalars have degree zero. Thus this is an actual map of sheaf Hom complexes, with the fixed augmentations, not a comparison chosen solely for being invertible.

proof.text:
Compute the transpose of $d$ before localization. On the total-tensor summand with $m\in P^i$, $x\in Q^r$ it is
$$(m\otimes b)\otimes(x\otimes s)\longmapsto(-1)^{ir}j(q(x)(m)\otimes bs).$$
The sign occurs because the order is $P\otimes\mathcal Hom(P,I)$; with Hom first it is absent. The representative evaluation and its fixed localized augmentation are exactly [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation], with the normalized tensor model of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. The ordinary scalar-association map first sends the same tensor to $(m\otimes x)\otimes bs$, and applying scalar-extended $R$-evaluation followed by $j$ gives precisely the same formula. Equality on every sheafified pure-tensor summand gives equality of these chain maps: tensor relations and sheafification extend equal maps uniquely. Consequently their localizations, followed by the identical inverse augmentations, agree. Derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes the scalar functor on $P,Q$. Here $I\otimes_RS$ represents $TN$ because tensoring with the finite free $S$ is, after restriction, a finite direct sum; it preserves the quasi-isomorphism to $I$. No assertion that $I\otimes_RS$ is K-injective is made: that is the role of $J$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $P\otimes_RS$ and $Q\otimes_RS$ remain flat-term K-flat over $S$, so the displayed total tensor also computes the derived tensor on the target side.

proof.text: The transpose computed in Step 3 is the pairing defining $c_{M,N}$ in [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change]. The tensor-Hom bijection is injective, so $d=c_{M,N}$ as $S$-linear derived morphisms, and $d$ is invertible by that node. This argument also proves independence of the resolutions used to describe $d$: every such description has that same transpose. In particular no inference of equality from restriction of scalars, from finite-level evaluations, or from an isomorphism of limit objects is involved.

proof.text: Unfold the recorded scalarHomCompleted and scalarHomCompleteInputs constructions. The completed comparison is the inverse Hom-output completion isomorphism, followed by scalarHomOrdinary, followed by the internal-Hom image of the inverse first-input and direct second-input completion isomorphisms. Cancel the Hom-output completion map to obtain the first displayed comparison identity. Composing with the opposite input identifications cancels both input maps by functoriality, proving specifiedHomIdentified = scalarHomOrdinary. The ordinary map is defined as the closed transpose of scalar-extended evaluation; apply the inverse transpose and its inverse law. This proves specifiedHomScalarEvaluation directly from the actual construction. Steps 2--4 separately establish its representative chain normalization.

proof.text: Suppose now that $H$ is bounded constructible. The coefficient-operation theorem places $CM,CN,CH$ in the integral constructible domains, so all the established maps can be rationalized. The rationalization definition keeps objects and tensors each Hom group with the coefficient field; it preserves an equality, its composites and its inverses. The rational internal-Hom action in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is bilinear: $H(a\otimes c,b\otimes d)=H(a,b)\otimes cd$, with the first input contravariant. Thus an integral naturality equality for an input map remains true after multiplication by a scalar, and expanding finite sums proves it for arbitrary localized morphisms in either input. In particular a denominator $t^{-r}$ acts through its image in $L$, which is invertible even when $L/E$ is ramified. Applying this to Step 5 and to the unit/tower equations proves the asserted identities in the raw rationalized categories. No idempotent completion or perfectness assumption is used. The theorem specifiedHomScalarRationalEvaluation itself is definitionally the localization of scalarHomCompleted: integralHomScalarComparison is its full-subcategory lift, and scalarHomCompleted is exactly the three-completion-unit conjugate displayed on the right. Thus this evaluation clause is proved by reflexivity, independently of the remaining rational naturality and coherence assertions.
